correctness.rationale: The calculation was independently reconstructed. The centered Euclidean regular simplex has the required orthogonal symmetry, so its gnomonic lift has spherical centroid exactly at the north pole. The centroid halfspace cap is the exact homothetic simplex with scale \(m/(m+1)\), giving the sharp Euclidean ratio. Dirichlet barycentric moments give \(E\|X\|^2=m^2/(m+2)\); scaling covariance and adding the cap centroid gives a cap-minus-full second-moment difference \(-m^2(m-1)/[(m+1)^2(m+2)]\). Expanding the exact gnomonic density \((1+\varepsilon^2\|y\|^2)^{-n/2}\) therefore gives normalized coefficient \(m^2(m-1)/[2(m+1)(m+2)]\) in \(\varepsilon^2\). Since \(m\varepsilon=\tan\rho\), this is exactly \((n-2)/(2n(n+1))\). The remainder is uniform on the fixed compact simplex.
